deliverables.runtime_conflict_rule: Installer/preflight reports the .NET Desktop Runtime and any known CoreCLR add-in version conflict before loading; it never downloads a runtime from inside Excel.

rules: Pure Python and .NET packages have no Excel, ETABS, COM, HTTP server, UI or rendering dependency.
Python retains Pydantic v2 as its sole base third-party runtime dependency for strict boundary models; NumPy, reports, PDF, DXF, CAD and ETABS remain extras.
The .NET contracts/core/code/member packages use the base class library and System.Text.Json; Math.NET is isolated to bounded analysis that needs it.
Excel-DNA exists only in StructuralEngineering.ExcelDna and CSI interop exists only in StructuralEngineering.Etabs.
Direct and transitive versions are locked for candidate builds; updates use a reviewed dependency packet with focused conformance/build/installed evidence by impact.
Each distributed artifact carries license inventory, SBOM, package-lock digest and known runtime prerequisites.
Optional adapter absence or version mismatch returns ADAPTER.UNAVAILABLE or VERSION.INCOMPATIBLE with detected/required versions and remediation.
No package performs runtime code download, implicit plugin discovery from untrusted folders or automatic host mutation.

deliverables.reference_floor: Windows 11 x64, 4 physical/8 logical CPU threads, 16 GB RAM, SSD, current .NET 10 patch; application classes additionally use 64-bit Microsoft 365 Excel and exact ETABS target. Results always record actual hardware/runtime/power mode.

budgets.workload: 10,000 warmed FO01-FO08/value or one-section code-kernel calls per operation, no serialization/trace
budgets.budget: per-call p95 <= 1 ms and batch elapsed <= 2 s; cold first pure-library operation <= 500 ms
budgets.memory: no unbounded growth; allocations reported per operation

budgets.workload: 1,000 ordinary rectangular section check sets and separately 100 complete ordinary single-span member evaluations, summary results
budgets.budget: section batch <= 1 s and complete-member batch <= 3 s in each native library

budgets.workload: 10,000 fixed-action candidates from a frozen catalogue/domain with complete required checks and summary results
budgets.budget: complete <= 5 s; first progress and cooperative cancellation acknowledgement <= 250 ms between non-interruptible kernels
budgets.memory: stream/prune summaries; incremental working set <= 512 MB

budgets.workload: 10,000 action rows plus identities round-trip strict JSON and canonical digest
budgets.memory: peak incremental working set <= 4 times UTF-8 payload size plus 64 MB

budgets.workload: typical 20-member/200-action-row standalone workbook calculation and controlled table write; separately cold XLL load
budgets.budget: warm command median <= 750 ms and p95 <= 1 s; cold XLL ready <= 3 s; progress/cancel response <= 250 ms
budgets.memory: Excel working-set delta <= 256 MB for workload

budgets.workload: small 100-member/10,000-row and medium 1,000-member/100,000-row getter, capture and offline normalization on the certified host
budgets.budget: small p95 <= 5 s and medium p95 <= 30 s; publish getter, transfer, normalization and persistence times separately
budgets.memory: incremental adapter working set <= 512 MB for medium workload

deliverables.claim_rule: A budget is a release acceptance target, not a measured current capability. Failure blocks that performance claim and triggers profiling/root-cause work; it never permits skipping correctness, completeness or reanalysis.
deliverables.trace_policy: Default operations return summaries and governing records. Full station traces, candidate tables, drawings and report rendering are requested explicitly and benchmarked separately.

method: Freeze workload JSON, semantic/profile/code-data revisions and correctness expectations before timing.
Run correctness/conformance first; discard no slow sample because its result differs.
Record machine, CPU/RAM/storage, power mode, OS, process architecture, Python/.NET/Excel/ETABS/XLL versions, source/artifact hashes and background-load policy.
Use at least 5 untimed warm-ups and 30 measured warm iterations for library/workbook workloads; report median, p95, maximum, allocation/working-set and raw samples.

Measure cold start in at least 10 fresh processes/Excel launches. ETABS live runs use enough repetitions to explain practical variation and retain each sample; they are never mixed with library timing.
Separate kernel, validation, serialization, COM transfer, workbook range I/O, rendering, save and ETABS analysis/acquisition times.
Compare Python and .NET on identical effective inputs, but report each against its own budget; language difference is not correctness evidence.
Check cancellation/progress with timestamped request/acknowledgement and identify any non-interruptible application call.

deliverables.artifact_identity: Record pre-sign build hash, signed artifact hash, signature certificate/timestamp identity and distribution-package hash. Reproducibility applies to unsigned managed inputs; signing is verified rather than expected byte-identical.
deliverables.publication_rule: Package publication, GitHub Release and public XLL distribution still require the repository's per-release owner authorization and release gates. PF9 does not grant it.
deliverables.support_diagnostics: A support bundle contains versions, hashes, structured diagnostics and redacted receipts; source models, workbook business data and personal paths are opt-in only.
